title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type equations for pairs (ξ,η) in the profinite free group Π_{0,3}^ (the profinite π1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}). ρ is the order-3 automorphism and σ_∞ the order-2 automorphism of the tripod. The previous page reduces the system to (145): ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 together with a loop relation involving the multiplier μ=2ν+1 (the cyclotomic-type parameter λ of GT).

This page, 'Le calcul adélique': Π_{0,3} is identified with the principal congruence subgroup Γ(2)/±1, generated by (1 2;0 1) and (1 0;2 1). Its profinite completion therefore maps to PSL(2,Ẑ) (written Sl(2,Ẑ)'). Grothendieck pushes ξ and η into PSL(2,Ẑ) and lifts them to SL(2,Ẑ). The lifts are defined only up to sign. On the first relation he writes:

- He normalises the sign of ξ via the cocycle relation (147): ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=±1.
- For η there is no comparable trick. Even granting provisionally that η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}, one gets a priori only (148) ησ_∞(η)=±1. Replacing η by −η cannot change this sign.

Write ξ=(A B;C D) and η=(R S;T U), both of determinant 1 (149). With ρ given by conjugation by an order-3 matrix r, (147) says (ξr)^3=±1. In each ℓ-adic component the eigenvalue/trace argument applies: g = ξr with g^3=±1 and g≠±1 forces tr g = ±1 (from g² = tg−1, g³ = (t²−1)g − t). After fixing signs this becomes the linear condition (150): C+D−B=1.

The only exceptional ℓ-adic solution is g=±1, i.e. ξ_ℓ = −ρ^{-1} = (1 −1;−1 0). Grothendieck cites a proposition on p.399 for this. That solution is excluded by ξ≡1 mod 2 (A,D odd; B,C even). Hence (150) holds in every Z_ℓ, and so in Ẑ.

Next page: since σ_∞(η^{-1}) = ᵗη, (148) reads η = ±ᵗη. The minus sign would force U=0, contradicting η≡1 mod 2. So η is symmetric (S=T). The loop relation then gives B=εS, D=εU and μD=1, so the SL2(Ẑ) images of (ξ,η) are pinned down linearly in terms of μ.

Purpose: determine the image of the GT-type data (μ,ξ,η) in the 'congruence/adelic' quotient SL(2,Ẑ). The upshot is that this image is essentially controlled by the multiplier μ. This is the 'calcul adélique' counterpart of the 'calculs abéliens' mentioned on the previous page.
errors: The duplicate equation number (148) is used for two different displays (the relation ησ_∞(η)=±1 and the matrix notation); this is cosmetic.
In (147) the correct relation, consistent with (145), is ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=±1, not ξρ(η)ρ²(η). The machine transcription misreads it.

The passage from (ξr)^3=±1 to the linear trace condition (150) needs the componentwise argument, since Ẑ is not a domain. Grothendieck handles this correctly via ℓ-adic components plus the mod 2 exclusion of the degenerate solution. The bookkeeping of the sign ± versus the trace sign is left implicit and is partly corrected in a marginal 'Oups' on the next page.

ideas.what: Map Π_{0,3}^ = F̂_2 ≅ Γ(2)^/±1 → PSL(2,Ẑ), and analyse GT-type equations after projection to SL(2,Ẑ) ('adelic computation')
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT / the Drinfeld associator f in the congruence completion of Γ(2); the action of GT on congruence quotients factoring through the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Galois action on congruence quotients); Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura and others on GT and modular towers (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or La Longue Marche as an explicit computation, as far as known (unsure)

ideas.what: Sign/lifting ambiguity PSL2 → SL2, resolved by congruence conditions mod 2 (ξ,η ≡ 1 mod 2)
ideas.modern_name: Lifting from PSL2(Ẑ) to SL2(Ẑ) using the level-2 structure

ideas.what: The order-3 relation (ξr)^3=±1 converted into a trace condition tr(ξr)=±1, componentwise ℓ-adically
ideas.modern_name: Elements of order 3/6 in SL2 over Z_ℓ, characterised by trace

ideas.what: σ_∞ acting on the SL2 image as inverse-transpose, so the 2-cocycle condition makes η symmetric
ideas.modern_name: Involution of SL2 induced by the complex-conjugation-type symmetry

deep.surprise_reason: This is an explicit, essentially routine computation of the projection of the GT/loop equations to SL(2,Ẑ) via Γ(2). It is consistent with later known results that GT acts on congruence quotients through its cyclotomic parameter. It is a nice archival detail showing Grothendieck doing the 'adelic' check, but it contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: (147) should read ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = ±1 (dans Sl(2,Ẑ)), not ξρ(η)ρ²(η).
'qui viennent en des éléments' probably reads 'qui relèvent en des éléments' (lifts from Sl(2,Ẑ)' = PSL to SL).
'Il y a une ambiguïté de signe, qui se lève pour ξ en imposant' (not 'qui lie pour').
'(lien en une admettant la possibilité d'écrire' probably 'même en admettant provisoirement la possibilité d'écrire η ∈ Π_{0,3} sous la forme βσ_∞(β)^{-1}'.
The marginal diagonal note probably reads roughly: 'mais ici on a le droit de faire ξ ≡ +1 mod 2 ... (mais alors une convention de signe différente de celle ...)'. It is only partly legible.
The second '(148)' is a duplicate number for the matrix notation.
'(des racines dans chaque composante ℓ-adique ...' is likely '(dans chaque composante ℓ-adique, il n'y a qu'une seule exception à cette relation, soit ξ_ℓ = −ρ^{-1} ...'.
The last line: '(150) est vrai dans Z_ℓ pour tout ℓ, donc dans Ẑ'.
